Kākāpō breeding season smashes records

Jane Smith, Reporter

Conservation staff say this year's kākāpō breeding season has produced more chicks than any season since intensive management of the flightless parrot began in the 1990s.

The Department of Conservation said 82 chicks had survived to fledging across the four predator-free islands that make up the recovery programme, comfortably beating the previous record set in 2019.

Programme manager Deidre Vercoe said a heavy rimu mast had given breeding females the food they needed, and new artificial insemination techniques had lifted fertility rates among the small and genetically limited population.

Rangers will now spend the winter monitoring the juveniles, fitting transmitters and deciding which birds are moved to new sites to ease pressure on existing islands.
